long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Detroit to Benson and Edith Ford, Alandt grew up within the third generation of the Ford family. She later became president of her parents' charitable fund. Her governance work at Henry Ford Health, The Henry Ford museum and the Detroit Zoological Society has linked family resources to institutions across southeast Michigan.

Alandt has chaired the Eleanor and Edsel Ford House and spent more than 25 years on the College for Creative Studies board, where she serves as vice chair. Her work combines preservation of the Ford family's historic estates with grants for arts, education and healthcare. The college awarded her an honorary degree in 2026 for that sustained civic and cultural contribution.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 99. ShipbuildingHistory directly names Lynn and Paul Alandt as Onika's owners; Florida's official registry independently links Lynn F. Alandt and Paul Alandt to Onika Corporation in distinct officer roles. Ford, CCS, Ford House, Henry Ford Health, TIME and the wedding notice converge on the same Lynn McNaughton Ford Alandt.

The Delta yard list is a specialist secondary source rather than an official ownership registry. Its direct naming is nevertheless reinforced by the official Onika Corporation filing, the unusual Onika name, the shared Grosse Pointe Shores geography, Delta's repeat-owner chronology and the authoritative vessel record.

The authoritative relationship starts in September 2011, while Delta and SuperYacht Times report the yacht's 2014 delivery. The earlier date may represent a contract, construction or database relationship date; no reviewed source resolves the convention, so the dates are excluded from the biographies.

Superyacht Network reports Onika at 40.5 metres and 499 GT, while SuperYacht Times reports 39.62 metres and 499 GT and Delta markets the yacht as 133 feet. The difference likely reflects length conventions and does not impair the name, builder, delivery-year or tonnage match.

Paul D. Alandt is Lynn's husband and an adjacent independent owner record. The 2026 Ford proxy explicitly identifies him, not Lynn, as minority owner of two Ford and one Lincoln dealerships. Those dealerships are excluded from Lynn's wealth mechanism, biography and tags. Shared Onika and foundation records are used only where they name Lynn directly.

Ford's 2026 proxy reports 6,262,583 Class B shares and 8.84 percent beneficial ownership for Lynn F. Alandt, but its footnote includes individually held, fiduciary or co-trustee holdings and spouse-held shares. The dossier therefore describes a beneficial family holding rather than treating every share as unrestricted personal property.

Inherited is supported by Alandt's Ford-family lineage and substantial current Class B stake, not by a public probate record. The reviewed sources do not establish the exact estate, trust, gift or other transfer sequence by which she acquired each beneficial interest, so the biography avoids a precise mechanism.

The Benson and Edith Ford Fund and the Lynn and Paul Alandt Foundation are separate charitable entities. Their reported assets are not treated as Lynn's personal wealth. The former supports her own current presidency; the latter is retained only to distinguish Lynn's and Paul's separately reported officer roles.

The surname field is proposed as Alandt because official current sources use Lynn F. Alandt and the wedding notice establishes Ford as her birth surname. McNaughton Ford is proposed as the middle-name content to preserve the fully evidenced birth and family names, while the public display Lynn Ford Alandt remains unchanged.
TIME's 1951 notice supports Detroit and the birth year but does not give an exact day or month. No birth-day or birth-month proposal is made, and the upstream calculated age is not used as evidence.

Ford is the only proposed active tag. It satisfies the catalogue's principal-family-owner contract through her current Class B holding.
